simple: the card you fill in for one device before writing any driver code.
analogy: the visitor card at reception.
precise: a design-log entry with the fields identification, class and catalog row, documentation tier, documents found, observation needed, design note, test plan and status; the runbook forbids driver code for a device without one.
source: C1 of F4-14 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two numbers every PCI device answers with: who made it, and which product it is.
analogy: the country on a passport and the passport number.
precise: 16-bit fields at configuration offsets 0x00 and 0x02; vendor IDs are assigned by PCI-SIG to members, device IDs are chosen by the vendor; a read of 0xFFFF from the vendor field means no function answered.
source: C1 of F4-14 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); L3 of F4-14 (/usr/include/linux/pci_regs.h (linux-libc-dev 6.8.0), opened in this build: register offsets and bit names used by …); D2 of F4-14 (PCI Local Bus Specification and PCI Express Base Specification (PCI-SIG): configuration space, configuration mechanism …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a second pair of numbers naming the board or laptop maker's variant of a chip.
analogy: the school badge a visitor wears in addition to the passport.
precise: Subsystem Vendor ID and Subsystem ID at offsets 0x2C and 0x2E of a type-0 header; quirks and firmware choices are often keyed on them.
source: C1 of F4-14 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); L3 of F4-14 (/usr/include/linux/pci_regs.h (linux-libc-dev 6.8.0), opened in this build: register offsets and bit names used by …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: three bytes saying what kind of device this is, independent of who made it.
analogy: "this visitor speaks French" rather than "this visitor is Ms Dupont".
precise: base class, subclass and programming interface in configuration bits 31:8 of offset 0x08, defined by the PCI Code and ID Assignment Specification; for example 01 08 02 is an NVMe controller.
source: C1 of F4-14 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); D1 of F4-14 (PCI Code and ID Assignment Specification (PCI-SIG): class codes (curriculum item 91)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one PCI device slot that contains several separate functions, each with its own IDs.
analogy: the delegation that signs in as a group.
precise: a device whose function 0 has bit 7 of the header-type register set; functions 1–7 must then be probed too.
source: L3 of F4-14 (/usr/include/linux/pci_regs.h (linux-libc-dev 6.8.0), opened in this build: register offsets and bit names used by …); R5 of F4-14 (Devicetree of QEMU's AArch64 virt machine (fdt_virt.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the names firmware gives devices that cannot announce themselves.
analogy: the head teacher's guest list.
precise: ACPI objects in the device's namespace scope: _HID names the device (a PNP ID such as PNP0501 or an ACPI ID such as ACPI0013), _CID lists IDs of standards it is compatible with.
source: C1 of F4-14 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); D3 of F4-14 (ACPI Specification (UEFI Forum): "Device Configuration" chapter (_HID, _CID, _CLS, _ADR, _CRS), AML encoding, …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the devicetree's way of naming a device, as text.
analogy: a list of languages, the best-spoken first.
precise: the compatible property, a list of "vendor,device" strings, most specific first; a driver binds to the first entry it knows.
source: C1 of F4-14 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); D4 of F4-14 (Devicetree Specification (devicetree.org): flattened blob format, compatible) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a file that turns numbers into names.
analogy: the directory of countries and schools at reception.
precise: community-maintained lists such as pci.ids (used by lspci) and usb.ids, and the registry of PNP and ACPI vendor prefixes (pnp.ids locally); they are a lookup aid, not a specification.
source: L1 of F4-14 (/usr/share/misc/pci.ids (Version 2024.03.31) and usb.ids (2024.03.18), opened and read by Listings 2–3 in this build; a …); L2 of F4-14 (/usr/share/hwdata/pnp.ids, opened and read by Listing 3 in this build) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number from 1 to 6 saying how much is known about programming a device, and where it comes from.
analogy: phrasebook, letter from the visitor's school, a colleague's notes, nobody, a sealed envelope.
precise: the curriculum's table 5.2: 1 open class standard, 2 public vendor documentation, 3 documentation only under NDA, 4 open driver only, 5 only a closed driver, 6 locked.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one driver that works for every device following a published standard.
analogy: a French teacher who can help any French-speaking visitor.
precise: a driver bound by class code, interface class or compatible ID rather than by vendor and device ID, for example NVMe (PCI class 01 08 02) or USB HID (interface class 03); vendor-specific differences are handled as quirks.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R1 of F4-15 (Boot trace on q35 (university/labs/F4-15/build.log, boottrace.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a known difference between what a device should do and what it does, with its workaround.
analogy: "this visitor nods when they mean no".
precise: a table entry keyed by IDs, subsystem IDs, revision or firmware version (or SMBIOS strings for whole machines) that changes driver behaviour for that device; the runbook asks for evidence with every entry.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the vendor's list of known mistakes in a chip.
analogy: the visitor's school writing "our guide is wrong on page 12".
precise: a document published per chip and stepping (Intel "specification update", Arm "Software Developer Errata Notice", NXP "chip errata"); read with the datasheet.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: documents you may only read after signing a secrecy contract.
analogy: a letter marked "for staff of the partner school only".
precise: tier 3; for an individual it is the same as tier 4, and the runbook forbids using NDA or leaked material even when the learner has it.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the text file that tells Windows which devices a driver package serves.
analogy: an interpreter's business card listing every language they speak.
precise: a driver package's setup information file: its models section lists every hardware ID the package supports, and it names the service (.sys) it installs, registry parameters and often firmware files.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a time-stamped log of what started during boot, including which driver took which device.
analogy: the morning register of which interpreter met which visitor, and when.
precise: in the curriculum, a Windows performance trace whose driver-load events give .sys names, order and timing; in this lab, the kernel's own log with a time-stamp-counter value per line.
source: C1 of F4-15 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R1 of F4-15 (Boot trace on q35 (university/labs/F4-15/build.log, boottrace.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: learning how to talk to a device by watching a program that already can, without copying that program.
analogy: the teacher in the corner with her own notebook.
precise: stage (c) of the method: observe a working driver at the hardware boundary (register reads and writes, bus transactions, USB requests), write a specification in your own words, then implement from it; the curriculum calls it lawful interoperability reverse engineering.
source: C1 of F4-16 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one person watches and writes the rules, another person who never saw the original writes the new driver from those rules.
analogy: the phrasebook passed to a teacher who was never in the room.
precise: a stricter variant that separates observer and implementer; historically used to keep implementations independent of the observed code.
source: C1 of F4-16 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a list of every read and write a driver makes to a device's memory-mapped registers, in order, with values.
analogy: the notebook's lines: "said this, heard that".
precise: produced on Linux by mmiotrace for a driver on real hardware, or by an emulator or hypervisor that traps each access (QEMU's memory_region_ops_read/write trace events in this lab).
source: C1 of F4-16 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R2 of F4-16 (Filtered trace (trace.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: read all the registers you safely can, let the working driver do one thing, read them again, and compare.
analogy: photographing the classroom before and after one lesson.
precise: read-only dumps around a single action; shows which registers that action changed, not how; reads with side effects (read-to-clear status) make it unsafe on some devices.
source: C1 of F4-16 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the document you write from your notes, saying only what you saw.
analogy: the phrasebook.
precise: a register-by-register and sequence description in your own words, with every statement traceable to evidence and every gap marked "unknown"; the input to the design note (F4-17).
source: R4 of F4-16 (spec_observed.txt, written in this build from R1–R3) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: writing one register changes what another register reads.
analogy: saying one phrase makes the visitor change their answer to a different question.
precise: in a trace, a write at offset A followed by a read at offset B that differs from B's previous read, with no write to B in between; the usual sign of command, status and acknowledge registers.
source: R3 of F4-16 (Annotation (annotate.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the written plan for a driver, made before the code.
analogy: the interpreter's plan for the visit.
precise: one entry per row of the curriculum's table 5.4, each with its answer and "where found"; plus a register table giving every register's source document and section title; approved by the learner before driver code (runbook).
source: C1 of F4-17 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the driver's first meeting with a device: check it really is what it claims, then take charge of it.
analogy: the greeting at the gate.
precise: the driver-model function called after a match; it claims resources, runs the initialization sequence and a self-test, and returns an error (leaving the device unbound) if any check fails.
source: R1 of F4-17 (Driver run (university/labs/F4-17/build.log, driver.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device disappears while the driver is using it.
analogy: the visitor who goes home at lunch without a word.
precise: on PCI Express, reads after removal return all ones (the curriculum's 5.4 "Error handling" row); in this build's emulator, a BAR whose memory decoding is off reads 0 instead, which a status poll can mistake for "done".
source: C1 of F4-17 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R3 of F4-17 (Version 1 under the same fault (forensic.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: waiting for a device, but never forever.
analogy: "wait ten minutes, then report".
precise: a poll or sleep loop with a deadline (here in time-stamp-counter ticks), whose expiry is a distinct, reported error; the curriculum asks for "timeouts on every wait".
source: C1 of F4-17 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a write the CPU sends without waiting to hear that it arrived.
analogy: a note pushed under the door.
precise: PCI memory writes are posted: they may still be on their way when the next instruction runs; a read from the same device forces earlier writes to complete first, which is why drivers "read back to flush" when order matters.
source: C1 of F4-17 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); D2 of F4-17 (PCI Local Bus Specification and PCI Express Base Specification (PCI-SIG): command register, ordering rules for posted …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of every register the driver uses, with where each fact came from.
analogy: the plan's list of rooms, each with who holds its key.
precise: the part of the design note that M2's acceptance test checks: "Each register the driver touches is listed in the design note with its document and section title."
source: C1 of F4-17 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of tests a driver must pass, written before the tests are.
analogy: the rehearsal programme agreed before rehearsing.
precise: the document of stage (e): emulator tests (or why none exist), host unit tests, trace-replay tests, the real-hardware matrix, fault injection, soak and reference comparison, each with its acceptance criterion; criteria are fixed there and not weakened later without the learner's approval.
source: C1 of F4-18 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small stand-in for the kernel functions a driver calls, so the same driver code runs in a normal program.
analogy: the colleague who plays the office during a rehearsal.
precise: host implementations of mmio_read32, rdtsc, the PCI accessors and printing, sending device accesses to a model and giving a deterministic clock.
source: R1 of F4-18 (Host unit and fault tests (unit.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that behaves like the device, for testing.
analogy: the colleague playing the visitor from a script.
precise: here, a host class implementing the observed specification's behaviour of each register, with switches that inject faults; it models what was observed, not what a datasheet promises.
source: R1 of F4-18 (Host unit and fault tests (unit.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: playing a recorded conversation with the device back to the driver and checking it says the same things.
analogy: replaying last year's real visit line by line.
precise: every read returns the recorded value, every write must equal the recorded offset and value; any difference is a mismatch.
source: C1 of F4-18 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R3 of F4-18 (Trace replay (replay.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: break the driver on purpose and check that the tests notice.
analogy: sending a deliberately bad interpreter to the rehearsal.
precise: a mutant is a copy of the code with one small change (here, the busy-wait removed); a suite that passes on a mutant is too weak to protect against that kind of bug.
source: R6 of F4-18 (Mutation check (mutation.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: run the driver for a long time and count errors.
analogy: a full-day rehearsal, not five minutes.
precise: long runs (the curriculum says hours) with throughput and error counters logged; this build's soak is 20,000 operations in the emulator.
source: C1 of F4-18 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R5 of F4-18 (Soak (soak.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the curriculum's big table of every kind of device and where to learn about it.
analogy: the office folder with one page per language.
precise: section 6.1 of the Systems Curriculum: one row per device class with interfaces and standards (issuing body), open documentation, reference drivers (Linux · BSD · Windows) and notes on honest scope; the entry point to stage (b).
source: C1 of F4-19 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one line of the catalog, for one class of device.
analogy: one page of the folder.
precise: a class such as "NVMe" or "I2C, SMBus, I3C and sensors", with its documents and drivers; the device record's "class and catalog row" field names it.
source: C1 of F4-19 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the organisation that writes and publishes a standard.
analogy: the association that publishes a language's official phrasebook.
precise: for example PCI-SIG, USB-IF, NVM Express, the UEFI Forum, JEDEC, MIPI Alliance, IEEE, OASIS; several restrict current editions to members or sell them, which the catalog's "Open documentation" column says.
source: C1 of F4-19 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a working driver in another OS, read to learn and to compare.
analogy: another school's interpreter whose notes you may read.
precise: the catalog's fourth column, naming drivers in Linux, the BSDs and Windows (Windows binaries are closed and studied through the Windows Driver Kit documentation and samples).
source: C1 of F4-19 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list, for one machine, of every device with its row, tier and driver status.
analogy: the visitor list for the week with an interpreter planned for each.
precise: the result of 6.2: "Add a line to your design log for each device: class row, tier, driver status. That list is your real-hardware roadmap for the machine."
source: C1 of F4-19 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first boots of your system on a new machine, done to find out what works.
analogy: the head's first walk through the new building.
precise: a staged boot that records CPU, memory map, firmware tables and devices and binds what it can, with every step logged; C12's goal is "Boot your loader and kernel on the spare machine; inventory its devices; make storage, network and input work on the real controllers."
source: C1 of F4-20 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the wire your kernel's messages travel on, so you can read them on another computer.
analogy: the phone line from the new building to the old office.
precise: C12 asks for "A serial or network log path for debugging (a USB-to-serial adapter, a PCIe serial card, or a network log sender after C9)"; the ACPI SPCR and DBG2 tables name a machine's console and debug ports.
source: C1 of F4-20 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: tables in the firmware where the machine says its own make, model and firmware version.
analogy: the plaque at the building's entrance.
precise: the DMTF System Management BIOS tables: an entry point ("_SM_" or "_SM3_") and typed structures (type 0 firmware, type 1 system, …), each with a formatted area and a set of strings.
source: D1 of F4-20 (DMTF System Management BIOS (SMBIOS) Reference Specification); R2 of F4-20 (Boot on q35 with -smbios strings and -device edu (boot.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a fix that applies only on machines with a certain maker and model name.
analogy: "in this building, the third-floor door sticks: push hard".
precise: a quirk table entry keyed by SMBIOS strings (system or baseboard maker, product, version, firmware version); the curriculum names Linux's DMI-based quirks as the reference.
source: C1 of F4-20 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how long each step of the boot took.
analogy: the times on the head's clipboard.
precise: per-stage durations from a time source (here time-stamp counter ticks, not converted to seconds), compared between boots; C12's last acceptance line asks you to compare yours with a Windows boot trace of the same machine.
source: C1 of F4-20 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: making sure a device is there before waiting for it.
analogy: knocking once and listening before waiting at a door.
precise: a read whose "nothing here" value is known (on this lab's machine, 0xFF from an unclaimed I/O port) tested before any wait loop that the absent value would keep busy.
source: R3 of F4-20 (Boot on q35 with i8042=off (boot_nops2.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way for an input device to send keyboard and mouse style messages over a small two-wire bus.
analogy: the visitor in room 2C and her notes.
precise: Microsoft's "HID over I2C Protocol Specification": a device on an I2C bus exposes a HID descriptor at a register named by ACPI (_DSM), from which the host learns the registers for the report descriptor, input, output and commands; ACPI identifies it with compatible ID PNP0C50.
source: D1 of F4-21 (Microsoft, "HID over I2C Protocol Specification"); C1 of F4-21 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the card a HID device hands over describing what its messages mean.
analogy: the shorthand card.
precise: a byte string of items (main, global, local; each a one-byte prefix with tag, type and size, then 0, 1, 2 or 4 data bytes) defined by the USB-IF HID class definition; the same descriptor format is used on USB, I2C and other transports.
source: D2 of F4-21 (USB-IF, "Device Class Definition for Human Interface Devices (HID)" and "HID Usage Tables" (including the digitizer …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one message from the device: button states and positions packed into bits.
analogy: one note from room 2C.
precise: a byte string whose fields the report descriptor locates by bit offset and size; on HID over I2C it is read from the input register and starts with a 2-byte length.
source: D1 of F4-21 (Microsoft, "HID over I2C Protocol Specification") — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: on I2C, the silence that means "nobody here" or "not now".
analogy: knocking on a door and hearing nothing.
precise: the receiver leaves the acknowledge bit high after an address or data byte; an I2C controller driver reports it as an error (the lab's model returns -ENXIO, which this course recalls, unverified, as the value Linux I2C drivers use for an address NACK); C14 requires that "A deliberate wrong I2C address produces a reported "no acknowledge" error, not a hang."
source: D3 of F4-21 (NXP, UM10204 "I2C-bus specification and user manual"); C1 of F4-21 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an interrupt that keeps firing as long as the signal stays on.
analogy: a bell that rings as long as the button is held.
precise: the interrupt condition is the line's level, not its change; the device holds the line asserted until the cause is cleared (for a HID-over-I2C device, until the host reads the pending report), so a handler that does not clear the cause is called again at once.
source: D1 of F4-21 (Microsoft, "HID over I2C Protocol Specification") — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the line in the ACPI table that says which GPIO pin carries a device's interrupt.
analogy: the bell board's wiring chart: which bell is room 2C.
precise: an ACPI resource descriptor in a device's _CRS naming a GPIO controller, pin, trigger mode and polarity; with I2cSerialBusV2 (controller, address, speed) it is how the touchpad's ACPI object tells the OS how to reach it.
source: D4 of F4-21 (ACPI Specification (UEFI Forum): I2cSerialBusV2 and GpioInt resource descriptors, _DSM); C1 of F4-21 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way for the processor to rest when there is nothing to do; deeper rests save more but take longer to wake from.
analogy: standing at the desk, sitting in the back room, going up to the staff room.
precise: a C-state (C0 running, C1 halt, deeper states with caches or voltages reduced); the platform lists the states it supports through ACPI _CST or _LPI or through a processor-specific driver.
source: C1 of F4-22 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); D2 of F4-22 (ACPI Specification (UEFI Forum): processor power states (_CST, _LPI), performance control (_PSS, _PCT, _PPC, _CPC), …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how long it takes to wake up from a rest, and how long the rest must last to be worth it.
analogy: the walk back down from the staff room, and how long the afternoon must stay quiet to make the walk pay.
precise: per-state figures an idle governor uses: a state is chosen only if the predicted idle time is at least its target residency and its exit latency is within what the system tolerates.
source: D3 of F4-22 (Linux kernel documentation, "CPU Idle Time Management" and "CPU Performance Scaling") — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the small program that decides how deep to rest each time.
analogy: the receptionist's guess about the quiet.
precise: C15's "idle governor choosing between halt and deeper states from expected idle length"; Linux has menu, ladder and others.
source: C1 of F4-22 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); R6 of F4-22 (Governor model (governor.log)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a speed setting for the processor: faster uses more power.
analogy: how many classrooms are open.
precise: a P-state, chosen through ACPI _PSS/_PCT/_PPC, through CPPC (_CPC), or by hardware within limits the OS sets (Intel HWP, AMD CPPC); the delivered frequency is measured with the APERF/MPERF ratio.
source: C1 of F4-22 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a temperature at which the system must act.
analogy: the marks on the thermometer.
precise: ACPI thermal zones define passive trip points (reduce performance), active ones (turn on a fan) and a critical one (shut down); C15 requires that "A simulated critical trip point (test build) triggers an orderly shutdown with file systems synced."
source: C1 of F4-22 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)); D2 of F4-22 (ACPI Specification (UEFI Forum): processor power states (_CST, _LPI), performance control (_PSS, _PCT, _PPC, _CPC), …) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: counters inside the processor that add up how much energy it has used.
analogy: the school's electricity meter.
precise: Intel's Running Average Power Limit interface (energy status counters and power limits in MSRs, in the SDM's power and thermal chapter); C15's acceptance uses package energy from RAPL at idle.
source: D1 of F4-22 (Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Volume 3, power and thermal management chapter (MWAIT …); C1 of F4-22 (Systems Curriculum, a map, not a source (AH-4)) — pending verification (sources title only, dossier gate G1 open)
